flashcards.q: When should you use SSE vs WebSocket for LLM token streaming?
flashcards.a: SSE over fetch() POST for one-directional token delivery (the 90% case) -- stateless, no sticky sessions, works through standard proxies. WebSocket only when the client must send data mid-stream (interruption, approval gate, collaboration).

flashcards.q: Why can't the browser's native EventSource API be used for an authenticated LLM chat endpoint?
flashcards.a: EventSource only supports GET requests with no custom headers and no request body, so it can't send a POST body (message history) or an Authorization header. Real implementations use fetch() with a ReadableStream reader instead.

flashcards.q: What is the SSE frame format?
Does SSE have transport-level backpressure like WebSockets?
flashcards.a: No. SSE has no flow-control signal from consumer back to producer -- the server keeps writing regardless of client consumption. WebSockets have real backpressure via bufferedAmount and TCP's receive window.

flashcards.q: Why batch token-delta rendering on requestAnimationFrame instead of calling setState per token?
flashcards.a: A frame budget is 16.7ms at 60Hz; per-token setState with an expensive render tree (markdown parse, syntax highlighting) can fall behind a fast model and stutter or freeze the tab. rAF decouples network arrival rate from render rate and self-paces to the display refresh rate.

flashcards.q: What does AbortController.abort() actually stop, and what does it NOT guarantee?
flashcards.a: It rejects the pending fetch() promise (AbortError) and closes the TCP connection. It does NOT guarantee the server stops generating/billing tokens -- that requires the server to explicitly listen for the connection-close event (e.g. req.on('close')) and cancel the upstream model call.

flashcards.q: Why must TextDecoder.decode() be called with { stream: true } when consuming a chunked stream?
flashcards.a: Multi-byte UTF-8 characters (emoji, CJK) can split across network chunk boundaries. Without stream:true, an incomplete trailing byte sequence gets replaced with U+FFFD (corrupted text); stream:true holds incomplete bytes in decoder state and prepends them to the next chunk.

flashcards.q: How should optimistic tool-call UI reconcile a tool-call event with its later tool-result event?
flashcards.a: Key state by toolCallId and update the existing entry in place (status: running -> done, attach result) rather than appending a second, separate message -- this avoids the card flashing/remounting when the result arrives.

flashcards.q: A streamed response arrives all at once instead of incrementally, even though the server writes incrementally. What's the likely cause?
flashcards.a: A reverse proxy or CDN (commonly nginx) is buffering the response by default. Fix by disabling response buffering for the streaming route (X-Accel-Buffering: no header, proxy_buffering off).

flashcards.q: Why send periodic heartbeat comment lines (": ping\n\n") during a long silent tool call?
flashcards.a: Load balancers/proxies with idle-connection timeouts (commonly 30-60s) can't distinguish "still working, no output yet" from a dead connection and will kill it. A heartbeat every ~15s keeps the connection alive through shorter timeouts.

flashcards.q: What changed structurally in Vercel AI SDK v6 (May 2026) that made the v5->v6 migration a "silent" break?
flashcards.a: useChat's message shape moved to an interleaved parts model (text/tool-call/tool-result/reasoning as ordered array entries). Old code kept compiling against the new shape but consumed it incorrectly, since it's a structural change, not a renamed export.

flashcards.q: What determines LLM token arrival rate, and why shouldn't a frontend engineer treat it as a fixed constant?
flashcards.a: Model size, batch size/concurrency on the serving side, hardware, and decoding strategy (e.g. speculative decoding) -- not anything the frontend controls. Real production rates under load often differ from an unloaded local test, so buffering strategy should be designed against measured p95 inter-arrival time.

flashcards.q: Why is a message represented as parts: [...] (text-delta, tool-call, tool-result, reasoning) rather than a single string?
flashcards.a: A real agent response interleaves prose, tool calls, and post-tool-result prose in order; collapsing this into one string loses ordering and the ability to render tool-call cards distinctly from surrounding text.
